payload.title: One notification system: newsletters and subscriptions go through Caducus
payload.description:
**Decision (Ryan, 2026-11-12).** All notifications, newsletters and subscriptions included, go through ONE Caducus setup (AnthusAI/Caducus, docs/notifications-plan.md; the Papyrus `notifications` plugin is the client). The separate `newsletter` plugin (own subscriber table, roundup issues, approval, send ledger, panel, archive) converges: notifications owns subscribers and consent; the roundup/issue becomes a notification kind. Reusable parts are pushed DOWN into Caducus so every product gets them. Shipped and Distinctive Mark use the newsletter plugin today and must not break; Machines on Machines launches directly on the unified system.

**Goal.** One subscriber directory, one consent record, one send path, one suppression and pause story per site. The newsletter plugin is retired, not kept as a second system, and no shim is left behind.

**Stories.** Public audiences plus subscribe pages end to end; subscriber and consent ownership plus migration; issue/roundup as a notification kind; story-type selection with editor cuts; Analytics events; deliverability readiness; MoM launch. Separate story under PPY-1b83d3: the standardized quality ranking.

**Related, not duplicated:** PPY-4d1143 (notifications rollout), PPY-bbc8e5 (alert-list migration, alert lists only), PPY-c522bf (sending identity), PPY-f361ee (reader pages), PPY-819117 (SES events to EventBridge), PPY-19a098 (M2 issues, built in the newsletter plugin), PPY-99738c (compatibility shims, linked not duplicated).

**Order.** Public audiences, then ownership, then issue kind, then selection; deliverability and Analytics in parallel; MoM launch last.

**Acceptance.** Shipped, Distinctive and MoM send their roundups through Caducus; `src/papyrus_content/newsletter` subscriber, consent and send code is gone; each child story is accepted.
